stem: Which of the following is equivalent to \(2(x - 3)^{2} + 5(x - 3) - 12\)?
solution: Notice the repeated expression: let \(u = x - 3\). The expression becomes \(2u^{2} + 5u - 12\).
So the expression equals \((2x - 9)(x + 1)\). (Expanding both gives \(2x^{2} - 7x - 9\).)

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is \((2u - 3)(u + 4)\) with \(x\) written in place of \(u\); the result was never converted back using \(u = x - 3\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of a sign slip when substituting back; \((2x + 9)(x - 1) = 2x^{2} + 7x - 9\), whose middle term has the wrong sign.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of computing \(2(x - 3) - 3\) as \(2x - 3 - 3\) instead of \(2x - 6 - 3 = 2x - 9\).
explanation.D: Correct. With \(u = x - 3\), the expression is \((2u - 3)(u + 4) = (2x - 9)(x + 1)\).

verify:
x = symbols('x')
target = expand(2*(x - 3)**2 + 5*(x - 3) - 12)
assert target == 2*x**2 - 7*x - 9
assert simplify(value(choices[answer]) - target) == 0
assert all(simplify(value(choices[k]) - target) != 0 for k in choices if k != answer)
